title: Word order: eerst, dan and daarna
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/401f89e5e0fc81c68ac9ed0f2909da1c as of 2026-10-22T22:50:33.466Z: {"Bronhoofdstuk":2,"Hoofdstukken":["https://app.notion.com/p/401f89e5e0fc8113b4facf9a197eabed"],"Inhoudsstatus":"Aanwezig","Onderwerp":"Word order: eerst, dan and daarna","Ontbreekt":"","Type":"Grammatica","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/401f89e5e0fc81c68ac9ed0f2909da1c"} null Inversie: eerst, dan, daarna Eerst means first; dan and daarna mean then / after that. Use them to put the events in your city-trip message in order. ## Word order A Dutch main clause normally puts its conjugated verb in second position. If a time word or phrase comes first, the subject follows that verb. Time phrase + conjugated verb + subject + rest of sentence. - Eerst zijn we naar het museum geweest. — First we went to the museum. - Daarna hebben we gewinkeld. — After that we went shopping. - Dan hebben we mosselen gegeten. — Then we ate mussels. These three examples come from the archived exercise tips. Notice that zijn/hebben move before we; geweest/gewinkeld/gegeten remain at the end. ## Try it Rewrite each sentence with the given word first. 1. We hebben gewinkeld. → Daarna … 2. We hebben mosselen gegeten. → Dan … 3. We zijn naar het museum geweest. → Eerst … Answers 1. Daarna hebben we gewinkeld. 2. Dan hebben we mosselen gegeten. 3. Eerst zijn we naar het museum geweest. ## Sources and chapter links Source and related chapters English study explanation written from the examples and learning goals in archived chapter 2. This is a new learning aid; the archive does not contain the missing original grammar handout.
